outputs/teds/meta.json.completeness_rule: TEDS admissions in every year 2015-2023 and total admissions never change by more than 50% year to year (ratio within [0.5, 1.5])
outputs/teds/meta.json.method:
Phase 4b: TEDS-A treatment admissions as an independent, AREA-LEVEL signal on opioid addiction.

    python -m src.step_t            # panels, (a), (b), (c), (d), simulation coverage at actual panel sizes

Admissions are not prevalence: they count treatment episodes (not people) at publicly funded facilities,
depend on funding, capacity and referral practice, and miss office-based buprenorphine. Never joined to
NSDUH. TEDS-A here ends in 2023 (combined 2006-2023 file), so it covers the period BEFORE the main
decline in overdose deaths (late 2022 onward) and cannot test that decline itself.
outputs/teds/meta.json.scope: TEDS-A data here end in 2023, so they cover the period before the main decline in overdose deaths (late 2022 onward); they describe treatment admissions before and at the start of that decline and do not test the decline itself.
outputs/teds/meta.json.source: TEDS-A 2006-2023 combined PUF (SAMHSA), admissions 2015-2023; CDC VSRR state file (xkb8-kh2a) opioid deaths 'Opioids (T40.0-T40.4,T40.6)', Dec 12-month-ending; Census state population (intercensal 2015-2019, Vintage 2025 2020-2023)
outputs/teds/meta.json.teds_2024: TEDS-A 2024 is available from SAMHSA as a single-year file (released 2026; no combined 2006-2024 file) but is NOT included: these analyses use the combined 2006-2023 file and end in 2023.
